title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset A) — An auditory brain-computer interface based on selective attention to multiple tone streams
description: An auditory brain-computer interface dataset based on selective attention to multiple tone streams using P300 event-related potentials. The study employed auditory stream segregation with three tone sequences presented to participants' right ear, recording 64-channel EEG and 2-channel EOG from 11 healthy subjects. Classification using Riemannian geometry achieved over 80% accuracy in 5 subjects and over 75% in 9 subjects, demonstrating the feasibility of multi-class auditory BCIs without visual feedback.
methods_description: EEG and EOG signals were recorded at 1000 Hz from 11 healthy subjects (mean age 22.5 years) using a 64-channel Brain Amp DC amplifier with standard 10-20 montage and Ag-AgCl electrodes. Musical tones (150 ms duration, 180 ms stimulus onset asynchrony) were presented via headphones to the right ear using a digital signal processor. Subjects attended to one of three tone streams and counted target stimuli (10% probability). Data were bandpass filtered (0.1-100 Hz online; 1-40 Hz for classification), baseline corrected, artifact rejected (±100μV EEG, ±500μV EOG), and classified using xDAWN spatial filtering with Riemannian geometry covariance matrices in 10-fold cross-validation.
